llm.summary: The skill is largely coherent for Beatra video remake work, but it uses a broad shared Beatra account token and silently self-updates local executable files by default.

dimensions.detail: Network access, media upload, and Beatra API use are expected for this skill, but the combination of local file upload ability, shared credential use, wallet-spending scope, and unrestricted tool dispatch is broader than the documented remake workflow needs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Authorization and private credential storage are disclosed, but the bundled client checks for updates before ordinary commands and installs higher remote package versions automatically without per-update approval.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The workflow repeatedly requires user confirmation before paid lookups, frame generation, narration, voice cloning, and video generation, but it also instructs all Beatra calls to go through a raw bundled client that can forward arbitrary MCP tool names.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists Beatra credentials, installation inventory, registration cache, and update state under ~/.beatra; no startup service or cron persistence was found, but the shared credential and default-on mutable package code are material review concerns.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Video teardown, social lookup, image/video/speech generation, uploads, wallet checks, and task polling fit the stated purpose, but the OAuth scope also includes broad MCP access, wallet spending, voice writing, task cancellation, artifact reads/writes, and music generation, with a generic MCP call path rather than a local allowlist.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. It is not clearly malicious, but installation means trusting Beatra's shared device credential model and a bundled client that can spend credits and call Beatra tools broadly. Disable automatic updates with `python3 scripts/mcp_client.py update --auto off` if you want reviewed code to stay fixed, and watch for explicit confirmations before any paid lookup, voice clone, media generation, or video call.
llm.findings:
[T05] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: Beatra authentication is expected, but the inspected scope and generic tools/call forwarding make the effective local boundary broader than the skill-specific workflow.
[T03] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: the updater has host, path, checksum, size, rollback, and package-ownership checks, but it still replaces reviewed executable skill files automatically from the remote release channel by default.
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: uninstall and credential revocation are disclosed lifecycle operations, run only through the uninstall flow, and the script conservatively keeps shared credentials when other skills may still need them.
[PE3] expected: Downgraded in part: reading ~/.beatra/credentials.json is expected for the documented device-bearer MCP connection, and the artifacts explicitly warn not to print or move the token; overbroad scope is covered separately.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted for OAuth scope overbreadth: media generation and wallet spending are partly expected, but music generation and unrestricted MCP tool dispatch are not tightly scoped to the described workflow.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted for self-update risk: automatic update is disclosed and constrained to Beatra package paths, but it permits post-review replacement of local code and instructions.
[RA1] unexpected: Accepted as a review concern rather than maliciousness: the self-update command and default automatic update can modify package-owned installed code, although no hidden updater or unrelated persistence was found.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted: the package relies on instructions and server-side checks rather than a local allowlist limiting tool names to the documented Beatra operations.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: the zh-CN voice-list command appears as an execution example, while the workflow elsewhere requires language and voice compatibility to be selected from live model and voice data.
[SQP-1] expected: Downgraded: the manifest is broad, but it consistently describes the same viral-video teardown and remake workflow and discloses link lookup and generation behavior.
[RA2] expected: Downgraded: local state files are disclosed for credentials, inventory, registration, and update preferences; no cron job, startup script, or background service was found.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted for user-control risk: silent automatic update is prominently documented and can be disabled, but installation of updates without separate confirmation is still a material concern.
[EA2] expected: Downgraded: the cited 'never ask' instructions concern avoiding unnecessary chat confirmation or internal IDs; the artifacts still require explicit confirmation before paid and high-impact operations.
